When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **7/10**, EXTREME vs VIX Spike Tier **1/4**, BROAD, backwardation inactive
Price and breadth signals flag stress while the options market stays calm. Trust the Crash Index for direction of risk and the VIX tier for timing, since the fear premium has not arrived yet.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **100**, STRONG BUY vs Regime score **76** with a risk off bias and CONTRACTION at **70%**
One signal says buy capitulation, the other says the cycle is rolling over. Trust the regime read for sizing now and the contrarian read as a setup that needs a washout to confirm.
⚠ These two disagree: Confluence T1 x JPY active (VIX backwardation plus yen safe haven flow) vs VIX backwardation flag inactive
The yen leg is firing while the VIX term structure leg is not. Trust the yen flow as an early warning and wait for the VIX curve before treating it as a full signal.
Today's tension
Crash Index screams **7/10** while the VIX spike detector sits at tier **1** of **4**
Bull
Options markets are not pricing a vol expansion yet, with backwardation inactive and the spike tier at the bottom of its scale. The contrarian score of **100** says this selloff is already late enough to buy.
Bear
The Crash Index at **7/10**, a regime score of **76** and a CONTRACTION read at **70%** confidence all point down. US small caps are down **4.2%** in five days and crypto is down hard.
The tell: VIX term structure flipping into backwardation. That single move would bring the options market into line with the Crash Index and settle the argument in favor of the bears.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is under stress, and the options market has not caught up. The Crash Index reads 7/10, the regime score is 76 and four risk off signals line up. The S&P 500 is down 2.4% over five days and the Russell 2000 is down 4.2%. Yet the VIX spike detector sits at tier 1 of 4 with a 50% probability and no backwardation.

That gap tells you how to position. Cut gross exposure and trim small caps first, because they are leading the decline. Keep hedges on, but do not pay up for panic protection that the VIX curve is not asking for yet. The contrarian score of 100 gives you a reason to build a buy list, not to buy today. Capitulation needs a washout, and the CONTRACTION regime at 70% confidence says the washout may not be done.

The main risk is a fast move from calm to fear. Skew is already active, so the market is paying for downside. If VIX goes into backwardation, the Crash Index and the options market agree and you should expect a sharper leg lower. If the Crash Index drops while the VIX tier stays at 1, the stress is fading and the contrarian buy starts to carry weight.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime is CONTRACTION at 70% confidence, and the regime score of 76 puts you in the action zone with four risk off signals aligned. Growth is slowing and the market is repricing it.

In this regime you favor quality balance sheets, shorter duration risk and smaller position sizes, and you avoid chasing bounces in small caps. The contrarian score of 100 points to capitulation and inflation pressure, which means rallies can come fast and fail fast.

Use them to sell weak holdings. The reading that flips this stance is a drop in the regime score with breadth recovering and the Crash Index falling.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together have started to go their own way. Correlation drift is how far that relationship has shifted from its old level.

The composite zone is ELEVATED, with 55.8% of 43 tracked pairs diverging, and the divergence score sits at 100. The sharpest breaks tell the story.

Copper and gold went from a correlation of +0.86 to -0.13, so growth and fear are no longer pricing the same world. Gold and Treasury bonds moved from -0.53 to +0.67, so both are being bought together as safety.

Momentum against the S&P 500 fell from +0.84 to +0.33, and semiconductors against the S&P 500 fell from +0.91 to +0.45, so leadership is loosening. The pairs lean bullish 14 to 10 bearish, but the loudest breaks are the defensive ones.

Expect wider swings and less help from your usual diversifiers.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Weakness is concentrated in the US and crypto, and the rest of the world is holding up better. Korea's KOSPI leads Asia at +1.6% and Switzerland's SMI leads Europe at +1.6%, while the FTSE is up +0.9%.

Australia's ASX 200 is the Asian laggard at -3.0%. The S&P 500 is down 2.4% and the Russell 2000 is down 4.2%, so small caps are weaker than the index.

Crypto is the loudest signal: Solana is -8.2% and Ether is -9.8% over five days. That points to a liquidity pullback in risk assets that centers on the US.

For the US session, expect small caps and high beta to stay under pressure, and watch whether Europe's strength holds. If Europe turns down too, the move is global.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 7/10 · EXTREME — Crash imminent (rare Bonferroni signal)
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 7/10 and the VIX spike tier at 1 of 4 describe two different parts of the same market. The Crash Index reads price damage and internal weakness, and those are already deep.

The VIX detector reads whether options traders are paying for a vol expansion, and so far they are not: backwardation is inactive and the adaptive trigger is off. Only the skew flag is on, which means traders want downside protection but are not panicking.

That is a coherent state. Stocks have fallen, and the fear premium has not followed.

The usual way this resolves is that implied vol catches up to realized stress. You should treat the 50% spike probability as live, and watch the front of the VIX curve for the flip.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 7/10 — many signals aligned at once, the rare pre-crash configuration.

How to read

The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
